newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Top seeds move up in World Cities Chess.
newsitem.headline: Top seeds move up in World Cities Chess.

text.p: Three teams share the lead in the inaugural World Cities Chess Championship at the end of the third round on Wednesday.

Fourth seeds Oslo moved into a tie for first place after a comprehensive victory over an outranked Sydney team, the match highlight being a dramatic 24-move win by Norwegian Grandmaster Jonathan Tisdall against Sydney's Tim Reilly.
Tisdall triumphed despite leaving himself with only 20 seconds on his chess clock. Under the rules, a player who exceeds the time limit loses the game automatically.
"I thought I was heading for an endgame," said a relieved Tisdall after the game. "But when I reached the time control I suddenly noticed I was winning outright."
Oslo was joined in the lead by Ho Chi Minh City and outsiders Depok Margonda, but their real threat will come from Moscow and Donetsk, sitting just half a point off the pace.

Moscow, the top seed, recovered well from their surprise loss in the second round, outclassing Depok Kalapa, while second seeds Donetsk, after Moscow the only other all-Grandmaster team, took revenge on Moscow's vanquisher, Mandaluyung.
The only major surprise of the third round was the defeat of third seeds Tashkent by one of the many impressive Indonesian entries, Bandung.
The fourth and fifth rounds of the World Cities Championship will be played on Thursday, with the tournament concluding on July 14.
